provenance.note: R5 version-bump re-validation of pystatistics.mixed at the 5.0.0 major release. The mixed public API is unchanged from 4.5.7: lmm(y,X,groups,...), glmm(y,X,groups,family=...,...) and grm_lmm(y,X,random_factor,backend=...,reml=...,force=...) have identical signatures; family still accepts a family string; the .se->.standard_errors and .ci->.conf_int field names (migrated at 4.0) are the live spellings and the drivers already use them; grm_lmm is called with the low-rank factor positionally (no W= kwarg). No driver edits were required. All CPU studies were re-run live on 5.0.0 and reproduce the 4.5.7 numbers within their published tiers: LMM fixed effects to ~1e-16..3e-13 and logLik ~1e-11 (TIGHT tier), SEs / Satterthwaite df / variance components / BLUPs <=8e-5 (OPTIMIZER tier) vs lme4/lmerTest; LMM hard-cases match lme4's behaviour and singular diagnostics; GRM matches rrBLUP (beta <=3.4e-7, variances <=2e-5, h2 <=9.3e-6, BLUP corr = 1.0); GLMM matches glmer(nAGQ=1) (fixed effects+logLik ~1e-3, SEs/z/varcomp/BLUP ~1-5% Laplace tier), the gaussian/gamma free-dispersion fail-loud (A6) still fires, and the singular-RE collapse classifier still matches glmer isSingular. The grm_lmm MPS fp32 GPU leg was RE-RUN live on 5.0.0: the CF-1 no-silent-wrong gate holds (silent_wrong_count = 0; cond(W) <= 3e3 accepted, |dh2| <= 1.4e-3; cond(W) >= 1e4 refused loud) and MPS remains a correctness/portability path (0.36-1.0x vs fp64 CPU, not a win). The CUDA (Forge) grm_lmm GPU studies are CARRIED FORWARD from 4.5.7 (no CUDA host available on this run; the live MPS fp32-Gram gate re-proves the same fp32 defect-class behaviour). Hosts: powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU fp64 + Metal/MPS fp32; R lme4 1.1.38 / lmerTest 3.2.0 / rrBLUP 4.6.3; numpy+R Apple Accelerate); forge (NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti — CUDA evidence carried forward). Verdict: BLESS-CLEAN, no open findings, no behavioural change vs 4.5.7. See findings_ledger.md.
provenance.baseline: R5 version-bump: 4.5.7 (module complete, blessed) → 5.0.0 (major release, mixed API + numerics unchanged; rename-only surface confirmed already-migrated). CPU + MPS re-run live and reproduce 4.5.7; CUDA carried forward.

forge.device: NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti (CUDA fp32/fp64, compute capability 12.0)

reference.name: R lme4::lmer / lmerTest::lmer (LMM) + lme4::glmer (GLMM, Laplace nAGQ=1) + rrBLUP::mixed.solve (GRM)
reference.what: lme4::lmer for LMM point estimates, SEs, variance components, logLik and BLUPs; lmerTest::lmer for the Satterthwaite df/p lme4 omits; rrBLUP::mixed.solve (GBLUP/GRM, K = W Wᵀ / M, Z = I) for grm_lmm. Two honest LMM tolerance tiers (near-machine fixed effects; optimizer-bound variance components); GRM log-likelihood not compared across engines (different additive constant).

studies.title: LMM correctness vs lme4 / lmerTest — two-tier contract (REML + ML)
studies.note: Identical float64 inputs to both engines. TIGHT tier: fixed-effect β to ~1e-16..3e-13 and logLik/REML criterion/AIC/BIC to ~1e-11. OPTIMIZER tier: SEs, Satterthwaite df, p-values, variance components and BLUPs to <=1.3e-4 (lme4 bobyqa vs L-BFGS-B). REML and ML both, across random slopes+correlation (sleepstudy), crossed (Penicillin), simple (Dyestuff), singular (Dyestuff2) and nested (Pastes). coef_max_rel is the fixed-effect headline; varcomp_max_rel/blup_max_scaled are the optimizer-tier headlines. Dyestuff2 is is_singular on both engines.

studies.title: LMM hard-case behaviour match vs R (R10) + default invocation (R15)
studies.note: Adversarial grid (RIGOR R10): pystatistics matches R's BEHAVIOUR, incl. its singular-fit diagnostics. hc1 (perfect intercept/slope correlation → 2×2 boundary) is is_singular on both, with the boundary warning; hc2 (unbalanced groups with singletons) and hc3 (extreme variance ratio, ICC≈0.99999 — converges and matches R to 6.9e-6 after the 4.5.1 F3 fix) hold; hc4_nested_correct matches lme4's nested fit to machine precision, hc4_naive_crossed is the MATCHED reused-inner-label footgun (both engines treat it as crossed). R15: the bare lmm(y,X,groups) default equals the explicit (1|group) spec and matches lmer (recorded in the run config).

studies.title: GRM / low-rank model correctness vs R rrBLUP::mixed.solve
studies.note: grm_lmm(backend='cpu') vs rrBLUP::mixed.solve (K = W Wᵀ / M) across h² ∈ {0.2,0.5,0.8} and two sizes. Estimable quantities compared directly: β ≤ 3.4e-7, genetic/residual variances ≤ 2.0e-5, heritability ≤ 9.3e-6, genetic-value BLUP correlation = 1.000000. Log-likelihood is not compared (rrBLUP uses a different restricted-likelihood additive constant; every estimate agrees regardless).

studies.title: GLMM correctness vs lme4::glmer (Laplace nAGQ=1) — two-tier contract
studies.note: glmm() vs glmer(nAGQ=1) on identical float64 inputs, matching the approximation order. TIGHT tier: fixed-effect coefficients + logLik/deviance/AIC/BIC agree to ~1e-3 or better. OPTIMIZER/LAPLACE tier: SEs, Wald z, variance components and BLUPs agree to ~1-2% (finite optimizer tolerance; the fixed-effect covariance is the Laplace Schur inverse at the mode). Grid: cbpp (binomial/logit, random intercept + 4-level fixed factor), grouseticks (poisson/log), glmm_slope_synth (binomial, CORRELATED random intercept+slope), cbpp_probit (probit link via a Family instance). (Bit-identical to 4.5.6 — A.3 does not touch the glmm path.)

studies.title: GLMM hard-case behaviour match vs glmer (R10) + default invocation (R15) + fail-loud (A6)
studies.note: R10 grid: hc1 quasi-separation (huge-but-finite slope, matches glmer ~4e-5); hc2 singular RE (no group signal — variance collapses to 0 matching glmer isSingular=True, though glmm exposes no is_singular flag, finding G6); hc3 unbalanced with singletons (~2e-4). R15: the bare glmm(y,X,groups,family='binomial') default equals the explicit (1|group) spec (0.0) and matches glmer's default variance to ~6e-5 (the 4.5.6 collapse fix). A6: gaussian and gamma raise ValidationError rather than returning wrong statistics.

studies.title: GLMM CPU vs glmer across sizes (priority 3 / R1)
studies.note: Binomial random-intercept GLMM, group-count sweep. After the 4.5.5 structure-exploiting solver there is NO complexity-class gap vs glmer — empirical exponent pystatistics ~O(n^0.48) vs glmer ~O(n^0.68). A residual constant factor (speedup 0.29x at G=25 rising to 0.63x at G=400/n=6000) is glmm computing more per fit than glmer defers — the two-stage nAGQ=0->nAGQ=1 Laplace, the in-fit fixed-effect SEs, and the robustness stationarity probe (a documented R2 cost, not a scaling defect). CPU-only (matching lme4/glmmTMB). BLAS: numpy and R both Apple Accelerate.

studies.title: LMM CPU vs R across sizes (priority 3 / R1) — with the A.3 analytic gradient
studies.note: The A.3 analytic θ-gradient (4.5.7): the batched single-factor optimizer supplies the exact gradient of the profiled deviance, ~2.3× fewer deviance evals. Random-intercept: pystatistics still MEETS-OR-BEATS lme4 at every size (~3–5×). Random-slope (correlated 2×2 RE, finding F4): now ~1.35× faster end-to-end than at 4.5.6 and competitive with lmerTest at small/moderate G (speedup_vs_r 1.97× at G=10 → 0.99× at G=100 → 0.52× at G=2000, up from 1.06×/0.73×/0.42×). The residual at-scale gap is the in-fit Satterthwaite df pystatistics computes that lmerTest defers — a documented R2 cost, not a complexity-class gap. Estimates unchanged. BLAS: numpy and R both Apple Accelerate.

studies.title: GRM fp32-Gram no-silent-wrong gate boundary — Forge (CUDA) (R12/R13)
studies.note: [CARRIED FORWARD from 4.5.7 (originally 4.5.1) — no CUDA host on the 5.0.0 run; the live MPS fp32-Gram gate re-proves the same fp32 defect-class behaviour on 5.0.0; not re-measured on CUDA.] The grm_lmm fp32 GPU path forms K = W Wᵀ / M in single precision (the CF-1 defect class). Sweeping cond(W) across the fp32 gate on CUDA, silent_wrong_count = 0: cond(W) ≤ 3e3 ACCEPTED and correct vs fp64 (|Δh²| ≤ 1.1e-3), cond(W) ≥ 1e4 REFUSED loudly (NumericalError). A true classifier — never accepts a biased fit (R12), never refuses a recoverable one (R9); the gate keys on the double-precision conditioning of W so it survives a torch upgrade (R14).

studies.title: GRM fp32-Gram no-silent-wrong gate boundary — Powerhouse (MPS) (R13)
studies.note: [RE-RUN LIVE on 5.0.0 — MPS available on this host.] The same CF-1 gate re-proven on Apple Silicon / MPS (R13 — a guarantee is regime-conditional and must be re-proven per device): silent_wrong_count = 0, cond(W) ≤ 3e3 accepted and correct (|Δh²| ≤ 2.3e-3), cond(W) ≥ 1e4 refused loud — identical classifier behaviour to CUDA.

studies.title: GRM GPU earns-its-keep + R11 isolation — Forge (CUDA) (priority 4 / R11)
studies.note: [CARRIED FORWARD from 4.5.7 (originally 4.5.1) — no CUDA host on the 5.0.0 run; the live MPS fp32-Gram gate re-proves the same fp32 defect-class behaviour on 5.0.0; not re-measured on CUDA.] grm_lmm earns its GPU path on CUDA (RIGOR priority 4): fp32 is 6.6× (n=5000) and 14.7× (n=20000) over the fp64 CPU, accepted fits correct to |Δh²| ≤ 2.1e-4. R11 same-precision pivot: gpu_fp64 is numerically EXACT vs CPU (|Δh²| ≤ 1.8e-8) but only 1.2–1.6× faster (consumer fp64 throughput) — a correctness option; the fp32 headline is precision + hardware, reported honestly.

studies.title: GRM GPU on MPS — correctness/portability, not speed (honest) — Powerhouse
studies.note: [RE-RUN LIVE on 5.0.0 — MPS available on this host.] On Apple Silicon / MPS the grm_lmm fp32 path is a correctness / portability path only: the CF-1 gate holds (see the MPS gate study) but it does NOT beat the fp64 CPU (0.27–0.74×). Reported plainly — the GPU speed story is CUDA, not MPS; a GPU path that ties/loses to the CPU is not dressed as a win.

record_fields.coef_max_rel: max relative difference vs lme4 over the fixed-effect coefficients (the near-machine TIGHT-tier headline)
record_fields.loglik_rel: relative difference vs lme4 in the log-likelihood / REML criterion (optimizer-bound but flat-near-optimum, ~1e-11)
record_fields.varcomp_max_rel: max relative difference vs lme4 over the (away-from-boundary) variance components (OPTIMIZER-tier headline)
record_fields.df_satt_max_rel: max relative difference vs lmerTest over the Satterthwaite denominator df
record_fields.blup_max_scaled: max |Δ| over the random-effect BLUPs, scaled by their RMS (optimizer tier)
record_fields.py_singular: LMMSolution.is_singular — pystatistics flags the fit as on the RE-covariance boundary (mirrors lme4 isSingular)
record_fields.r_singular: lme4 isSingular() on the same fit — the behaviour-match target (R10)
record_fields.speedup_vs_r: lme4/lmerTest wall-clock / pystatistics wall-clock on the same fit (>1 means pystatistics is faster)
record_fields.beta_max_rel: GRM: max relative difference vs rrBLUP over the fixed effects
record_fields.heritability_rel: GRM: relative difference vs rrBLUP in narrow-sense heritability h²
record_fields.blup_corr: GRM: Pearson correlation between pystatistics and rrBLUP genetic-value BLUPs (1.0 = identical ranking/scale)
record_fields.verdict: CF-1 gate outcome for an fp32 GPU fit at a given cond(W): accepted_correct / refused_loud / SILENT_WRONG (the last must never occur)
record_fields.dh2_vs_fp64: |Δh²| of an accepted fp32 GPU fit vs the fp64 CPU optimum (the no-silent-wrong check, R12)
record_fields.gpu_fp32_speedup_vs_cpu: fp64 CPU wall / fp32 GPU wall (>1 means the GPU earns its place, priority 4)
record_fields.gpu_fp64_speedup_vs_cpu: fp64 CPU wall / fp64 GPU wall — the same-precision hardware-only pivot (R11)
record_fields.gpu_fp64_dh2_vs_cpu: |Δh²| of the fp64 GPU fit vs the fp64 CPU — the hardware-exactness check (~1e-8)
record_fields.deviance_rel: GLMM: relative diff vs glmer in the conditional deviance (Σ deviance residuals² at the mode)
record_fields.z_max_rel: GLMM: max relative diff vs glmer over the Wald z-statistics
record_fields.failed_loud: GLMM R10: True if glmm raised ValidationError for a free-dispersion family (required A6 behaviour)
record_fields.py_var: GLMM hardcase: pystatistics RE variance (vs r_var — the singular/boundary behaviour-match)
